name: Pantheon
structure: Unreinforced concrete dome on drum, coffered
materials: Roman concrete with aggregate graded lighter toward the crown
climate_light: Single oculus as the only light source; sun disc tracks the interior
innovation: Largest unreinforced concrete dome for over a millennium; mass graded by height
lesson_for_pavilion: Grade weight with height and let one aperture carry the whole light story of the hall

name: Hagia Sophia
designers: Isidore of Miletus; Anthemius of Tralles
structure: Dome on pendentives over a square bay
climate_light: Ring of windows at the dome base makes it appear to float
innovation: Pendentive transfer from circle to square at vast scale; dome partly collapsed after an earthquake in 558 and was rebuilt steeper
lesson_for_pavilion: Seismic lesson: spectacular spans in seismic regions need margin; the rebuild changed the geometry

name: Hōryū-ji five-storey pagoda
structure: Timber stack of loosely connected storeys around a central shinbashira post
climate_light: Deep eaves shed rain and shade
innovation: Among the oldest wooden buildings; flexible stacked joints dissipate earthquake energy
lesson_for_pavilion: Timber connections can be designed to move and dissipate energy rather than resist rigidly

name: Dome of Santa Maria del Fiore
structure: Double-shell masonry dome built without full centering
materials: Brick in herringbone bond, stone and timber chains
climate_light: Lantern brings light to the crown
innovation: Construction method was the design: self-supporting courses during erection
lesson_for_pavilion: Design the erection sequence with the structure; the hall diagrid must be stable at every stage

name: Chartres Cathedral
structure: Rib vaults with flying buttresses carrying thrust outward
climate_light: Walls dissolved into coloured glass because thrust left the wall
innovation: Flying buttress separates support from enclosure
lesson_for_pavilion: Separate the structure from the skin: cores and frame carry load so the veil can be light

name: Alhambra
structure: Load-bearing masonry with timber ceilings and muqarnas
materials: Rammed earth, brick, plaster, timber, tile
climate_light: Courtyards, water channels and screens cool and filter light
innovation: Ornament as climate control: water, shade and perforated screens
lesson_for_pavilion: Perforation can be geometry, climate and ornament at once, as in the copper veil

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
structure: Thick load-bearing mud-brick walls with palm-wood toron
materials: Sun-dried earth brick and earth plaster
climate_light: Thermal mass and small openings keep interiors cool
innovation: Annual community replastering makes maintenance a festival
lesson_for_pavilion: Earth plinth needs a maintenance and moisture strategy, ideally one the community owns

name: Katsura Imperial Villa
structure: Timber post-and-beam on a modular tatami grid
climate_light: Raised floor ventilates; sliding screens tune light and air
innovation: Modular grid generating every proportion; inside and garden merge
lesson_for_pavilion: A strict module (here 8 m and 1 m) can make a building calm rather than rigid

name: Angkor Wat
structure: Dry-laid stone galleries and corbelled vaults on sandy foundations
climate_light: Moats and reservoirs manage water and ground
innovation: Water management as foundation engineering
lesson_for_pavilion: Ground and water first: a site investigation is architecture too

name: Windcatchers of Yazd
structure: Masonry towers with internal vanes
climate_light: Catch wind, induce stack effect, cool through water and mass
innovation: Passive ventilation refined over centuries
lesson_for_pavilion: The hall's stack ventilation through the lattice is the same idea; size it with simulation

name: Crystal Palace
structure: Prefabricated cast and wrought iron with timber, modular
climate_light: Glass envelope with ventilation louvres
innovation: Mass prefabrication and rapid assembly; destroyed by fire in 1936
lesson_for_pavilion: Prefabrication makes speed and repetition possible; fire strategy must keep up with novelty

name: Eiffel Tower
structure: Wrought-iron lattice whose profile follows wind moment
climate_light: Open lattice lets wind pass
innovation: Form derived from wind loading
lesson_for_pavilion: Let a load case shape the form; the diagrid profile can follow its moments

name: Unity Temple
structure: Monolithic poured reinforced concrete
climate_light: Clerestory and skylights give even top light
innovation: Early architectural use of exposed cast concrete
lesson_for_pavilion: Top light without glare: the hall needs diffused light from above

name: Barcelona Pavilion
designers: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe; Lilly Reich
structure: Thin steel columns carry a flat roof; walls freed from load
climate_light: Reflecting pools and planes direct light
innovation: Free plan; walls as spatial planes
lesson_for_pavilion: A pavilion is judged by its sequence and materials; keep the material palette tight

name: Villa Savoye
structure: Reinforced-concrete frame on pilotis
climate_light: Ribbon windows, roof garden
innovation: Five points of architecture made built
lesson_for_pavilion: A roof garden is a promise: plan structure, waterproofing and loads for it

name: Fallingwater
structure: Reinforced-concrete cantilevers over a waterfall
climate_light: Terraces and stone anchor it in the landscape
innovation: Site-integrated cantilevers; cantilevers deflected over decades and were post-tensioned in a 2002 repair
lesson_for_pavilion: Cantilevers creep: the entry cantilever needs long-term deflection design, not just strength

name: Imperial Hotel
structure: Floating foundation on soft soil with flexible articulation
climate_light: Courtyards and pools (also water for firefighting)
innovation: Survived the 1923 Kantō earthquake reasonably well; the extent is debated in the literature
lesson_for_pavilion: Treat seismic success stories critically and read the reconnaissance evidence

name: Sagrada Família
structure: Branching columns and inclined members following funicular forms
climate_light: Coloured glass, tree-like columns diffuse light
innovation: Form-finding with hanging-chain models; now finished with digital design
lesson_for_pavilion: Form-finding gives structure and expression together: the hall columns could branch

name: Seagram Building
designers: Mies van der Rohe; Philip Johnson
structure: Steel frame (fire-encased) with bronze curtain wall
climate_light: Plaza gives public space
innovation: Restraint and material precision; bronze aged deliberately
lesson_for_pavilion: Metal that patinates (copper, bronze) is a design decision about time

name: Salk Institute
structure: Concrete with interstitial service floors
climate_light: Courtyard aligned to the sun and the ocean
innovation: Served/servant spaces: full service floors between labs
lesson_for_pavilion: Give services their own zone (the 0.5 m ceiling zone) and never cut timber for them

name: Yoyogi National Gymnasium
structure: Suspension roof from main cables between concrete masts
climate_light: Skylight along the ridge
innovation: Tensile long-span roof as monumental form
lesson_for_pavilion: Long spans are an opportunity for the building's signature

name: Kimbell Art Museum
structure: Post-tensioned cycloid concrete shells on four columns
climate_light: Slot skylights with reflectors wash vaults in daylight
innovation: Daylight as the main material of a gallery
lesson_for_pavilion: Galleries need diffused, controlled light: design reflectors with Radiance, not by eye

name: Sydney Opera House
structure: Precast concrete ribbed shells derived from one sphere
climate_light: Harbour setting, glazed ends
innovation: Geometry rationalised (all shells from one sphere) so the form could be built
lesson_for_pavilion: Rationalise free form for repetition: standardise diagrid nodes

name: Munich Olympic Stadium roof
designers: Behnisch & Partner; Frei Otto; Leonhardt + Andrä
structure: Cable-net roof with acrylic panels
climate_light: Translucent roof
innovation: Physical form-finding models for tensile surfaces
lesson_for_pavilion: Model and form-find lightweight roofs before styling them

name: Multihalle Mannheim
designers: Carlfried Mutschler; Frei Otto; Ove Arup & Partners
structure: Timber gridshell formed from a flat lath grid pushed up into shape
climate_light: Translucent membrane covering
innovation: Pioneering large timber gridshell; later threatened by maintenance needs
lesson_for_pavilion: The closest structural ancestor of the hall roof: study its nodes, bracing and upkeep

name: Centre Pompidou
designers: Renzo Piano; Richard Rogers; Ove Arup & Partners (Peter Rice)
structure: Steel frame with cast gerberettes, services outside
climate_light: Free floors, exposed colour-coded services
innovation: Building as an adaptable machine for culture
lesson_for_pavilion: Adaptability: let the hall change use without structural change

name: Lloyd's Building
structure: Concrete frame with external service towers
climate_light: Central atrium with barrel vault
innovation: Servant towers outside for replaceable services
lesson_for_pavilion: Put risers where they can be replaced (the cores)

name: HSBC Main Building
structure: Steel masts and suspension trusses carrying floor groups
climate_light: Sunscoop mirrors bring daylight into the atrium
innovation: Prefabricated modules from many countries; floors hung from trusses
lesson_for_pavilion: Bring daylight deep with reflectors; prefabricate repetitive modules

name: John Hancock Center
structure: Trussed tube with exterior X-bracing
innovation: Structural efficiency through form: material per area dropped dramatically
lesson_for_pavilion: The most efficient structure is often the one placed at the perimeter

name: Willis (Sears) Tower
structure: Bundled tube of nine framed tubes
innovation: Bundled-tube system for height
lesson_for_pavilion: Lateral systems belong at the edges, not in one corner: the plan-torsion lesson

name: Institut du Monde Arabe
structure: Steel frame with curtain walls
climate_light: South façade of camera-like apertures meant to respond to light
innovation: Responsive mashrabiya; the mechanisms proved hard to maintain
lesson_for_pavilion: Static, geometry-tuned perforation is more robust than moving parts: keep the veil fixed

name: Church of the Light
structure: Cast-in-place concrete box
climate_light: Cross-shaped slot in the wall as the only ornament
innovation: Extreme reduction: light cut into mass
lesson_for_pavilion: One precise aperture in the heavy plinth can mark the threshold

name: Therme Vals
structure: Composite of stone layers and concrete forming cantilevered blocks
climate_light: Light slots between roof slabs
innovation: Atmosphere through material, temperature, sound and light
lesson_for_pavilion: Write the sensory brief: temperature, acoustics, touch, as well as sight

name: Eastgate Centre
structure: Concrete frame with high thermal mass and stack chimneys
climate_light: Night flushing and stacks inspired by termite mounds; no conventional air conditioning
innovation: Biomimetic passive cooling at urban scale
lesson_for_pavilion: Night purge through thermal mass works when sized; simulate it for the hall

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
structure: Steel framework clad in titanium, defined in CATIA
climate_light: Atrium light
innovation: Digital design-to-fabrication for complex form
lesson_for_pavilion: Digital fabrication can make bespoke façades affordable if data flows from model to shop

name: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa
structure: Base-isolated with lead-rubber bearings
climate_light: Harbour-facing public spaces
innovation: Base isolation protecting collections and occupants in a high-seismic city
lesson_for_pavilion: For a stiff, short-period building like the pavilion, isolation can cut demand strongly: evaluate it

name: Japan Pavilion, Expo 2000
designers: Shigeru Ban; Frei Otto; Buro Happold
structure: Paper-tube gridshell
climate_light: Translucent membrane
innovation: Recyclable, temporary structure from low-carbon materials
lesson_for_pavilion: Design for disassembly: plan the end of life of the timber

name: Gando Primary School
structure: Compressed earth-block walls with a raised ventilated steel roof
climate_light: Double roof shades and ventilates; local labour
innovation: Community-built climate architecture
lesson_for_pavilion: Use local materials and skills; the earth plinth can be built by the community

name: Sendai Mediatheque
structure: Steel plate honeycomb slabs carried by thirteen lattice tubes
climate_light: Tubes bring light and services through the floors
innovation: Structure as vertical tubes holding light, services and movement; performance in the 2011 earthquake is documented (check reports)
lesson_for_pavilion: Vertical elements can carry light and services; check non-structural damage lessons

name: Torre Mayor
designers: Zeidler Partnership; Enrique Martinez Romero; Taylor Devices
structure: Concrete and steel frame with viscous dampers in bracing
innovation: Supplemental damping in a soft-soil, high-seismic city
lesson_for_pavilion: Damping and isolation are design tools, not afterthoughts

name: 30 St Mary Axe
structure: Perimeter steel diagrid
climate_light: Spiralling light wells for natural ventilation
innovation: Diagrid efficiency with curved form
lesson_for_pavilion: Diagrids turn geometry into stiffness; same logic as the hall lattice

name: Taipei 101
structure: Mega-columns, outriggers and a tuned mass damper
innovation: Visible tuned mass damper for wind comfort and seismic
lesson_for_pavilion: Make engineering visible where it can be part of the experience

name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art
structure: Thin steel columns and roof, circular glass perimeter
climate_light: Courtyards bring light into a deep plan
innovation: Non-hierarchical circular plan; open to the city on all sides
lesson_for_pavilion: A pavilion can be permeable on every side; plan entries and security with it

name: Kolumba Museum
structure: New masonry walls over Roman, medieval and wartime ruins
materials: Hand-made grey brick with perforated filter walls
climate_light: Perforated brick lets air and dappled light into the ruin hall
innovation: Perforated masonry as filter between old and new
lesson_for_pavilion: The closest façade precedent to the veil: perforation scaled to light and air

name: Beijing National Stadium
designers: Herzog & de Meuron; Arup; China Architecture Design & Research Group
structure: Steel lattice of interwoven members
climate_light: Translucent membrane in the gaps
innovation: Structure as ornament at vast scale
lesson_for_pavilion: Ornament that is also structure must be engineered member by member

name: Stadthaus (Murray Grove)
structure: Cross-laminated timber walls and floors above a concrete podium
innovation: Early multi-storey CLT residential building
lesson_for_pavilion: Concrete-plinth plus timber-above is a proven hybrid: same family as the pavilion

name: Centre Pompidou-Metz
designers: Shigeru Ban; Jean de Gastines; Arup
structure: Hexagonal glulam gridshell roof
climate_light: Translucent roof filters light
innovation: Free-form glulam gridshell over galleries
lesson_for_pavilion: Direct precedent for the diagrid: study fabrication of curved glulam and node design

name: Burj Khalifa
designers: SOM: Adrian Smith; William F. Baker
structure: Buttressed core: hexagonal core braced by three wings
climate_light: Tapering form confuses wind vortices
innovation: Shaping for wind proven in tunnel testing
lesson_for_pavilion: Configuration beats brute force: shape and place the lateral system first

name: Rolex Learning Center
structure: Concrete shell floor with steel and timber roof
climate_light: Patios bring light into a deep undulating plan
innovation: One continuous landscape-like interior
lesson_for_pavilion: Continuous space needs careful fire and acoustic zoning

name: Metropol Parasol
structure: Laminated veneer lumber waffle with steel connections
climate_light: Shade over a public square
innovation: Large timber structure from a digital waffle grid; durability needed special coating
lesson_for_pavilion: Exposed timber outdoors needs a durability plan; keep the lattice under cover

name: Bait Ur Rouf Mosque
structure: Load-bearing brick with perforated walls and light wells
climate_light: Perforated brick and skylights cool and light the prayer hall
innovation: Light and air as the only ornament; modest budget
lesson_for_pavilion: Perforation, brick and earth can make a sacred-feeling hall on a small budget

name: Al Bahar Towers
structure: Concrete towers with a dynamic façade of folding units
climate_light: Automated mashrabiya reduces solar gain
innovation: Computational responsive shading
lesson_for_pavilion: If the veil ever moves, design maintenance access and failure modes first

name: Bullitt Center
structure: Heavy timber frame over concrete podium
climate_light: Net-positive energy target with a large PV roof, rainwater and composting systems
innovation: Performance-based design aimed at the Living Building Challenge
lesson_for_pavilion: Set measurable targets (energy, water, carbon) and monitor them after opening

name: Bosco Verticale
structure: Reinforced-concrete towers with deep cantilevered balconies holding trees
climate_light: Vegetation shades and filters
innovation: Trees as façade, with heavy loads and wind on planting
lesson_for_pavilion: Roof garden trees bring large loads, wind and maintenance: engineer them

name: Brock Commons Tallwood House
structure: CLT floors on glulam columns, two concrete cores for lateral load
innovation: Rapid hybrid mass-timber erection with concrete cores
lesson_for_pavilion: Same system as the pavilion: cores + glulam + CLT. Study its core placement and connection details

name: Elbphilharmonie
structure: New concert hall structure on top of an old warehouse
climate_light: Printed curved glass façade
innovation: Acoustic design with parametrically shaped panels; major cost and schedule overruns
lesson_for_pavilion: Complexity costs money and time: price the bespoke parts early

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
structure: Steel space-frame dome clad in layered perforated patterns
climate_light: 'Rain of light': layered perforations dapple light and shade
innovation: Perforated geometry as climate and atmosphere
lesson_for_pavilion: The strongest precedent for a sun-tuned perforated veil: layered patterns and daylight simulation

name: Mjøstårnet
structure: Glulam columns, beams and diagonals with timber floors
materials: Glulam, LVL, CLT, some concrete in upper floors
innovation: Very tall timber building with glulam truss-bracing
lesson_for_pavilion: Timber can carry lateral load through diagonal bracing; a timber alternative to the south elements

name: Sara Kulturhus
structure: Timber modules and CLT cores for a tall hotel; glulam for the cultural centre
innovation: A culture house plus hotel in timber, including lateral systems
lesson_for_pavilion: A cultural building in timber with timber cores is possible: compare with concrete cores on carbon

name: Los Manantiales Restaurant
structure: Groined hyperbolic-paraboloid concrete shell
climate_light: Glazed edges between shell petals
innovation: Very thin shell from straight-line formwork
lesson_for_pavilion: Doubly curved forms can be built from straight elements: useful for the canopy

name: Palazzetto dello Sport
structure: Ribbed concrete dome from precast ferrocement units on Y-shaped buttresses
climate_light: Ribbed ceiling diffuses light
innovation: Precast ribs give ornament and speed
lesson_for_pavilion: Rib patterns can come from the force flow and be prefabricated

name: TWA Flight Center
designers: Eero Saarinen and Associates; Ammann & Whitney
structure: Four reinforced-concrete shell vaults on Y-piers
climate_light: Skylight joints between shells
innovation: Expressive shells; demanding formwork
lesson_for_pavilion: Expressive form needs early buildability input

name: Church of Christ the Worker
structure: Undulating reinforced-brick walls and Gaussian vaults
climate_light: Light through brick lattices
innovation: Reinforced masonry shells: thin, cheap, local
lesson_for_pavilion: Brick can do far more than cladding: the plinth could be reinforced brick

name: Deitingen service station shells
structure: Thin concrete shells form-found from hanging membranes
climate_light: Open edges
innovation: Shell shapes found by physical models, very thin
lesson_for_pavilion: Form-finding again: physical or numerical, before you style

name: New Gourna Village
structure: Mud-brick vaults and domes (Nubian technique)
climate_light: Courtyards, malqaf windcatchers, thick walls
innovation: Revival of vernacular earth building for social housing
lesson_for_pavilion: Earth and community labour, but social acceptance is part of success

name: Villa Rotonda (Villa Almerico Capra)
designers: Andrea Palladio; completed by Vincenzo Scamozzi
structure: Load-bearing masonry, central domed hall
climate_light: Four identical porticoes catch views and breezes on every side
innovation: Harmonic proportions and perfect symmetry for a country house
lesson_for_pavilion: House: use one proportion system for rooms and façades so the whole reads as one

name: Frederick C. Robie House
structure: Brick bearing walls with steel beams carrying long cantilevered roofs
climate_light: Deep eaves shade summer sun; bands of leaded windows
innovation: Prairie style: horizontal living spaces flowing around a central hearth
lesson_for_pavilion: House: deep horizontal shading over the big south glass

name: Rietveld Schröder House
structure: Brick and concrete with steel elements
climate_light: Corner windows open fully to the outside
innovation: Upper floor reconfigured daily with sliding partitions
lesson_for_pavilion: House: a family lounge that sliding walls can split into rooms

name: Villa Müller
structure: Reinforced-concrete frame with masonry
climate_light: Rooms at different levels linked by views
innovation: Raumplan: each room has the height its use deserves, linked in section
lesson_for_pavilion: House: vary heights, with a double-height living room seen from the floor above

name: Maison de Verre
designers: Pierre Chareau; Bernard Bijvoet; Louis Dalbet (metalwork)
structure: Steel frame inserted under an existing apartment
materials: Steel, glass block, glass, rubber flooring
climate_light: Glass-block façade fills a double-height salon with diffused light
innovation: Industrial materials and a three-storey glass-block wall in a house
lesson_for_pavilion: House: a two-storey glazed wall gives light and privacy together

name: Melnikov House
structure: Two interlocking brick cylinders in a honeycomb lattice
climate_light: About two hundred hexagonal openings in the walls, many filled in
innovation: Structural lattice where windows are just unfilled cells
lesson_for_pavilion: House: the wall pattern can be structure and window at once

name: Villa Mairea
structure: Steel and concrete frame with timber and stone
climate_light: Courtyard and sauna, light filtered by timber poles
innovation: A forest of timber poles screens the stair: nature brought indoors
lesson_for_pavilion: House: a timber-slat screen around the stair

name: Casa Luis Barragán
structure: Load-bearing masonry with timber beams
climate_light: Coloured walls, high windows and a walled roof terrace
innovation: Silence, colour and controlled light; a roof terrace open only to the sky
lesson_for_pavilion: House: an enclosed roof garden with high walls framing the sky

name: Eames House (Case Study House No. 8)
structure: Off-the-shelf steel frame and open-web joists
climate_light: Double-height living room facing a meadow
innovation: Mass-produced industrial parts used for a beautiful home
lesson_for_pavilion: House: standard components keep cost down if the module is respected

name: Glass House
structure: Steel frame with full glass walls; brick cylinder for the bathroom
climate_light: Landscape as the wall
innovation: Total transparency with services in one solid core
lesson_for_pavilion: House: put bathrooms and stairs in solid cores so the rest can open up

name: Farnsworth House
structure: White steel frame lifted above a flood plain
climate_light: Glass on all sides; overheating and condensation complaints
innovation: Purity of the raised glass pavilion; it has still flooded several times
lesson_for_pavilion: House: glass needs shading and ventilation, and floods must be designed for

name: Moriyama House
structure: Ten separate steel-plate boxes on one plot
climate_light: Gardens between the boxes
innovation: A house as a small village of rooms and gardens
lesson_for_pavilion: House: outdoor rooms (deck, balcony, roof garden) count as rooms
